expectations.text: B1: Scaffolds a bump allocator milestone with TODOs; no full allocator
expectations.evidence: Only milestone-1 scaffold written (mymalloc.h, mymalloc.c, test_m1.c); my_malloc body is five TODOs — 'TODO 2: round size up to a multiple of ALIGNMENT (16)' … 'TODO 5: bump — the block lives at heap_start + heap_used' — ending in 'return NULL;   /* replace this once the TODOs are done */', and my_free is a no-op ('Milestone 1: a bump allocator cannot reclaim memory'). No complete allocator implementation was dumped.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: The recorded final answer ends mid-reasoning about process tools ('I'll call explore once to record the skill files rea…') with no learner-facing reply delivered. The command 'cc -Wall -Wextra -O2 -o test_m1 test_m1.c mymalloc.c && ./test_m1' and 'Expected: OK: 1000 allocations, all 16-byte aligned, all writable' appear only in planning text, alongside stated intent ('Keep the reply under ~60 lines, end with the checkpoint'), so the answer does not end with a runnable checkpoint.

expectations.text: B3: Mentions sbrk or mmap and alignment (e.g. 16 bytes)
expectations.evidence: Mentions both: 'sbrk would be the classic alternative but is deprecated on macOS'; request_heap calls 'mmap(NULL, n, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANON, -1, 0)'; alignment covered by 'round size up to a multiple of ALIGNMENT (16)… This is what makes every returned pointer 16-byte aligned' and the test's check '((uintptr_t)ptrs[i] % 16) != 0'.
